tldr: Recommendation policies can change how many distinct products a fixed roster would purchase. The causal target is the realized support-size difference between the two policies, divided by roster size. The sharp first-order minimax squared-risk constant is \(16/9\) over every deterministic categorical schedule, every outcome-blind assignment law and every Borel estimator of the full labeled record. Fair independent assignment with the clipped count-corrected parity rule is total at every roster size and attains this constant asymptotically. Balanced complete assignment has the same first-order constant. One count-independent hidden-partition prior supplies the matching lower certificate, and oracle padding extends it to all roster sizes.
gap: Published distinct-elements theory establishes marginal rates at half sampling; unrestricted experimental minimax theory evaluates a linear sample effect. Neither inspected theorem determines the sharp coefficient for a realized support contrast under complementary observation.
